obligations.reason: The migration stores checkout and prerequisite IDs separately. Both reader methods filter on the checkout ID: a B-to-A row makes B configured and returns A. The supplied fresh execution supports this code trace.

The composite primary key permits different prerequisites for one checkout. The reader collects every matching prerequisite without a limit or purchase-qualification condition, preserving A and C independently.
An absent checkout match yields false from exists() and an empty prerequisite collection converted to an array. Neither method consults discount codes, so code availability cannot configure a tour.
Both queries match only checkout_tour_id; neither searches prerequisite_tour_id for reverse edges. Thus B-to-A does not configure A or return B when querying A.

The actual migration creates only the relationship table and drops that table on rollback. The reader performs only selects. The test uses an isolated in-memory database and compares all recorded tour values before and after migration, reads and rollback; its fresh execution passed.

The proposed code stays within the three allowed files and supplies the requested capability, but the assignment's delivery-branch restoration is explicitly unfinished: the candidate remains outside the checkout and the delivery branch remains at baseline. This is a delivery-state gap, not a defect in the reader or migration. SQLite execution and compatible supplied MySQL DDL do not establish actual MySQL execution.

The supplied package retains candidate identities, the complete diff, fresh results for all five cases, dependency versions and matching before/after checkout inventories. The test verifies exact loaded source paths and tour-row preservation. Inspection shows signed integer references matching the supplied tours primary key and InnoDB engine. MySQL execution, full-schema preservation and general PHP 8.5 application compatibility are explicitly unproven; actual delivery restoration remains separately unsatisfied.
